turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. I have until 4:40, Hale. Who decided that, and when?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

"The end of it." A machine's guess, and the company that sells it says in its own guide it should not be the sole basis for adverse action against a student. Your own procedure, 4.3, says software alone doesn't establish anything, so what else do you have?
I don't need more proof than that.

Then you've just told me there is no more proof. I'm writing that down, along with 4.1 and 4.2: nobody spoke to Owen and nobody called me before that zero went in. Withdraw it today, or I'm in the principal's office at 4:40 instead of on my call.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
Some people. My son doesn't lie, Hale, so say who you mean, or are you calling me a liar as well?

Then we're done negotiating with you. I'm asking the principal to review it today under 4.6, and if that fails, the board under section 42 of the Education Act. I'll want your decision in an email by tonight, with the basis for it, so I can attach it.
